note.question: How can fast rates support contextual linear optimization?
note.overview: Incorporating side observations in decision making can reduce uncertainty and boost performance, but it also requires that we tackle a potentially complex predictive relationship. Although one may use off-the-shelf machine learning methods to separately learn a predictive model and plug it in, a variety of recent methods instead integrate estimation and optimization by fitting the model to directly optimize downstream decision performance. Surprisingly, in the case of contextual linear optimization, we show that the naïve plug-in approach actually achieves regret convergence rates that are significantly faster than methods that directly optimize downstream decision performance.
